text: Try tickling yourself right now. You can't. Your brain won't let you.
When someone else tickles you, your brain can't predict their fingers. Surprise!
But when you move your own hand, your brain sends a copy of the plan.
The cerebellum, at the back of your head, predicts exactly how it will feel.
And a touch you predicted gets turned down. Boring. No tickle.
Scientists in London tested this with a robot. You move it, it tickles you.
No delay? Barely ticklish. Add just a fifth of a second.
And it tickles more. Your brain guessed wrong, so it felt like someone else.
Did you just try to tickle yourself? Comment yes or no.
